title: WPSS/1104/2011 of DEEPAK KUMAR Vs UNION OF INDIA and OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No. 1104 of 2011
Honíble Rajiv Sharma, J.
Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. B.S. Parihar, Brief Holder for
the State.
The respondent no.2 published an
advertisement whereby the applications
were invited for filing up the post of
Constable (GD) in CISF, CRPF, BSF and
SSB. The petitioner was allotted roll
number. He appeared in the physical test
on 26.03.2011. He qualified the physical
test. Thereafter, he appeared in the
written test on 03.06.2011. He was
declared successful in the written test.
The call letter was issued to him. He was
asked to make himself available before
the Medical Board on 17.08.2011. The
petitioner once again called for appearing
before the Medical Board on 17.08.2011
at 7.00 a.m. However, he was not
medically examined for the simple reason
that the seal was not put on his caste
certificate. The petitioner insisted upon
the authorities that the caste certificate
was issued in accordance with the law.
The petitioner came back to his native
place at Roorkee. He obtained certificate.
He approached the higher authorities.
The higher authorities stated that his
candidature has already been cancelled.
The petitioner has not been treated in
just and fair manner. Petitioner belongs
to reserve category. His case should have
been considered in humane and fair
manner. The candidature of the petitioner
could not be cancelled merely on the
ground that the caste certificate issued to
him by the Competent Authority did not
have seal impression. Respondents have
raised a very hyper-technical view to
disprove the petitioner to get public
employment. The petitioner should have

been medically examined and even if
hypothetically, there was any
shortcomings, the petitioner should have
been permitted to remove the same.
 Accordingly, the writ petition is
allowed. The respondents are directed to
conduct the medical examination by
constituting a Special Board within a
period of eight weeks from today to
medically examine the petitioner. If he is
found medically fit, he may be offered
employment as Constable with all
consequential benefits.
Pending application, if any, stands
disposed of accordingly.
(Rajiv Sharma, J.)
17.02.2018
Jitendra
